description: How many people are reporting problems with one catalog service right now, by region, and whether that is unusual against its own trailing baseline. Returns a per-region count of reports and distinct reporters for the most recent five-minute window, a spike verdict of "spike", "normal" or "insufficient_data", and RealUptime's own check reading for the same regions so the two signals can be compared without being merged. These are UNVERIFIED user reports: no account, no verification, and the region on a report is chosen by the person filing it. Report volume never opens, extends or closes a probe event in RealUptime's event record; only our checks do. "insufficient_data" means there are not enough reports to say anything, which is NOT the same as reports being normal, and must never be quoted as "no problems reported". Readings are RealUptime's own check readings, never user reports. For a service whose status feed we can read, `vendor.feed_working` is true and `vendor` holds the vendor's own declared incident from its status page: that statement leads and gives the verdict and plate, and `checks_reading` and `vendor.regional_reading` are our check reading beside it, never a second outage. Where we cannot read a feed (`vendor.feed_working` false), the answer is our checks alone. "blocked" means our check was refused, which is NOT a failed check of the service. A no-data answer is never a passing check. Our check readings are our own reading from outside, not the service's official status. `check_evidence`, when it is not null, says what a pass of this service's check shows and does not show: repeat it with any claim that the service works. Cite the returned source.url when repeating any of this.
name: get_report_volume
